title: Stochastic transport of a Goldstone mode in a self-organized atomic crystal
authors: Zhanhai Yu, Di Xiang, Xiaotian Zhang, Hao Zhang
abstract: Spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry produces a massless Goldstone mode that can evolve across a degenerate manifold at zero energy cost. Goldstone modes have been identified primarily through excitation spectra, mode softening or collective oscillations. However, their time-domain transport under intrinsic fluctuations and dissipation has remained largely unexplored. Here we directly track the stochastic transport of a Goldstone mode in a self-organized atomic crystal inside an optical ring cavity. The ring cavity maps the order-parameter phase onto the real-space position of the emergent crystal. Without any external perturbation, fundamental photon-scattering recoil drives the collective transport, while cavity dissipation generates friction. We monitor individual trajectories of the atoms and their self-generated optical lattice by measuring the cavity output phase. We find that the diffusion constant decreases as $1/N$, indicating that all atoms move collectively as a rigid object rather than independently. By tuning the Langevin driving force and cavity-mediated damping, we show that the normalized diffusion constant collapses onto a single universal curve. This work extends the study of continuous symmetry breaking from excitation-frequency measurements to real-time tracking of transport, and opens routes for studying non-equilibrium collective transport, phonon dynamics, and defect formation in driven-dissipative quantum matter.
summary: This paper investigates the stochastic transport of a Goldstone mode in an atomic crystal coupled to an optical ring cavity. By measuring the collective motion of the lattice phase, the authors demonstrate that the atoms move coherently, showing diffusion scaling inversely with atom number. This work opens new avenues for studying non-equilibrium collective dynamics in quantum matter.
main_problem: The study aims to track the stochastic transport of a Goldstone mode, which emerges from the spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry, in a system subject to intrinsic fluctuations and dissipation.
main_result: The atoms move collectively as a rigid object, resulting in a diffusion constant that scales inversely with the number of atoms ($D \propto 1/N$), and the transport exhibits universal scaling behavior.
method: The research combines theoretical modeling (Langevin equations) with experimental measurement techniques, specifically monitoring the cavity output phase via heterodyne detection to track the center-of-mass motion.
model_or_system: The system is a self-organized atomic crystal formed by atoms coupled to an optical ring cavity. The physics is governed by a Hamiltonian exhibiting a U(1) symmetry that is spontaneously broken, leading to the Goldstone mode.
key_observables: Diffusion constant ($D$), cavity output phase ($\phi$), phase variance ($\Delta\phi^2$), and the normalized diffusion constant.
important_parameters: Atom number ($N$), damping coefficient ($	ilde{ eta}$), and the ratio of thermal energy to lattice depth ($k_B T/U$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the dispersive regime, the mean-field approximation, and the assumption that atoms move as a rigid body at low temperatures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ring-cavity setup mapping phase to position, show the transition to self-organized lattice, and demonstrate universal scaling of the diffusion constant versus damping and atom number.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model via the Hamiltonian and symmetry breaking, develops the Langevin equation for the collective coordinate, and then analyzes the resulting stochastic transport, culminating in measurements of scaling laws.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct, real-time measurement of Goldstone mode dynamics in a driven-dissipative setting, extending the study beyond traditional frequency-domain excitation measurements into non-equilibrium transport.
